questions.stem: When a catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction, then the rate constant (k) :

options.label: D
options.text: may increase or decrease depending on the order of the reaction

questions._flag: MY DERIVATION DISAGREES WITH THE OFFICIAL KEY, and the official key is kept as required. The marking scheme (ms idx 2) prints 10. (A) - 'remains constant'. A catalyst provides an alternative path of lower activation energy, and since \(k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}\), a lower \(E_a\) at the same temperature gives a LARGER k; NCERT Ch.3 says the catalyst 'alters the rate' by lowering \(E_a\), and the rate cannot rise at unchanged concentrations unless k rises. That points at option (C) 'increases'. A defensible reading behind (A) exists - that the rate constant OF THE UNCATALYSED REACTION is untouched, the catalyst merely opening a second pathway - but the stem asks about 'the rate constant (k)' of the reaction whose rate has increased. Recorded for a human; not resolved here. This is the ONLY one of the 16 Section-A answers where my derivation and CBSE's key differ.

questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.context:
The involvement of \((n-1)d\) electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) are common examples.
The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.

questions.context:
Proteins are the most abundant biomolecules of the living system. Proteins are the polymers of about twenty different \(\alpha\)-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. Ten amino acids are called essential amino acids. In zwitter ionic form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour as they react both with acids and bases.
On the basis of their molecular shape, proteins are classified into two types : Fibrous and Globular proteins. Structure and shape of proteins can be studied at four different levels i.e., primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary, each level being more complex than the previous one. The secondary or tertiary structure of proteins get disturbed on change of pH or temperature and they are not able to perform their functions. This is called denaturation of proteins.

It is kept as a single row rather than split into seven, because the printed mark allocation belongs to the question and no sub-part carries a mark of its own that the band would accept. The seven parts span four subtopics - (a) Nomenclature, (b) Isomerism, (c)/(d)/(g) and the spin half of (e) Bonding (CFT and VBT), (f) Definitions of Some Important Terms. Filed on 'Bonding in Coordination Compounds', which covers four of the seven.
